New York City. The most populous city in the United States, located at the mouth of the Hudson River on the Atlantic coast. It became a major colonial settlement in the seventeenth century and grew into a global financial, cultural, and artistic hub by the twentieth century.

The city was founded by the Dutch in sixteen twenty-four as New Amsterdam and remained a Dutch colony until sixteen sixty-four, when the English seized it and renamed it New York. Ellis Island, in New York Harbor, was the primary immigration gateway for millions of Europeans between eighteen ninety-two and nineteen fifty-four, making the city the doorway to America for countless immigrants. The Statue of Liberty, a gift from France, was dedicated in eighteen eighty-six and became the symbol of American freedom and hope for these newcomers.

Wall Street, in lower Manhattan, is the global center of stock trading and finance. The New York Stock Exchange was founded there in eighteen seventeen and established the city as an economic powerhouse. Manhattan's grid street system, laid out in eighteen eleven, revolutionized urban planning and influenced city design worldwide.

Broadway has been the heart of American theater since the early twentieth century, producing musicals and plays that define popular entertainment. The city hosted the first modern Olympic Games held in an American city in the nineteen twenties and nineteen thirty-two, and continues to host major cultural institutions like the Metropolitan Museum of Art.

New York shaped American identity, literature, and popular culture more than any other single place. The Jazz Age flourished in nineteen twenties Harlem and Manhattan, inspiring literary works like F. Scott Fitzgerald's The Great Gatsby, set in Long Island near the city. Walt Whitman's epic poem Leaves of Grass, celebrating American democracy, was written while living in Brooklyn. The city remains a global financial, cultural, and artistic hub that continues to influence the world.
